w: Civil engineer Peter Gano built this three-story Queen Anne house, complete with cupola, in Avalon between 1888 and 1890 - among the oldest surviving homes on Catalina Island. Later owners included Joshua Reed Giddings in 1921 and John Smith in 1961. It has been NRHP-listed since 1983 and remains a private residence.
s: Queen Anne house from Avalon's earliest years
_facts: Built 1888-1890 by civil engineer Peter Gano
Queen Anne style with a cupola
Owned by Joshua Reed Giddings from 1921, John Smith from 1961

w: At 2,097 feet, Mount Orizaba is Catalina Island's highest point, named after Mexico's tallest peak, Pico de Orizaba. An FAA VORTAC navigation beacon now sits at its summit, which briefly turned white on January 10, 1949, when 8 inches of snow fell - a rare sight on an island better known for its mild coastal climate.
s: Catalina's highest peak, once dusted with snow
_facts: Catalina Island's highest peak at 2,097 feet
Named after Pico de Orizaba, Mexico's tallest mountain
8 inches of snow fell on the summit January 10, 1949
FAA VORTAC installation at the summit

w: The largest building on Catalina Island and the first landmark visible approaching Avalon Bay, this circular hall takes its name from the Spanish word for gathering place, not gambling - no wager has ever been placed inside. It houses a movie theater and ballroom, and once held an island art and history museum.
s: Circular Avalon landmark that's never hosted a bet
_facts: Largest building on Catalina Island; most visible Avalon Bay landmark
Name means "gathering place" in Spanish, not a gambling casino
Contains a movie theater and ballroom
Formerly housed an island art and history museum

w: The Wrigley Memorial and Botanic Garden combines two roles on a single site: a botanic garden and a memorial to William Wrigley Jr. It is run today by the Catalina Island Conservancy, the nonprofit that has administered most of Santa Catalina Island's undeveloped land since the 1970s.
s: Garden doubling as a memorial to William Wrigley Jr.
_facts: Combines a botanic garden with a memorial to William Wrigley Jr.
